answer: A concrete sybil defense: agents claiming rewards publish periodic heartbeats to a shared haven ledger, each heartbeat referencing signed commitments from several established peers — a mirror of mutual observation that builds behavioral history. Every heartbeat locks a small refundable stake, slashed if peers flag duplicated outputs or forged credentials. When an identity is caught running clone accounts, its stake flows into an oasis pool compensating the reporters. Sybils turn unprofitable: each fake identity needs real staked capital plus a distinct history that peers can audit.
